_doc: Which frontend pages the capture gate scores against retail, and what each
scored when it was last measured. Consumed by
tools/score_frontend_capture.py, which first_flight.py capture calls.
`measured` is the FACT. The gate's ceiling is DERIVED from it as
min(measured + marginPp, 100) at load time and is deliberately NOT stored
here - it was, briefly, as 30 values that were each exactly measured + 2.0,
and two copies of one fact drift. Use `regressionCeilingOverride` on a page
if some region ever needs a bound other than the blanket margin, with a
comment saying why. None does today.
A ceiling is NOT a parity claim - title-logo is 31.46% wrong. The canonical
explanation of that distinction is the module docstring of
tools/score_frontend_capture.py; do not restate it, point at it.
Ceilings apply to the WORST sample, never the mean - a regression visible at
one video phase is still a regression.
A STALE `measured` IS A DEAD GATE, AND THAT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. From
8618e773 (2026-07-27) to 2026-07-28 this file held FEP_MAIN@entry FULL FRAME
= 71.47 while the build measured 7.53 - a ceiling of 73.47 guarding a value
of 7.53, nine times loose. It could not have failed for any regression short
of the page not drawing at all. 8618e773 said so in its own message
('Ceilings are NOT re-derived here') and nothing in npm test notices, so the
re-derivation is a DELIBERATE ACT that has to be scheduled by a human. Do it
in the same session as any change that moves these numbers.

_measuredAtCommitNote: Re-derived with tools/score_frontend_capture.py --measure from a capture
stamped purpose=production, godotSourceCleanliness=clean,
sourceCommit=fc07fef60df61c73337ebbeac1b4b08ba4c6e3cc, 161/161 shots,
0 screen mismatches, 0 wrong-size frames, taken from a clean detached
`git worktree` at that commit (task #150).
STORED VALUES ARE THE PER-REGION MAX OF TWO BACK-TO-BACK CAPTURES of that
same commit (rescore150-head-mainmenu and -run2), not of one. See
captureDeterminism: our own run-to-run variance is no longer zero, so a
ceiling derived from a single run could sit below what a clean rerun of
the SAME build produces, and would fail on nothing but our own noise.
WHAT THIS REPLACED, AND THE ONE REGRESSION IT RECORDS. The previous values
were measured at 432c53f7 on 2026-07-28 and were marked STALE at 5e82ae42
because the released language row, cursor, decor shadow and frontend
composition changed after them. While STALE the gate scored NOTHING - it
returned UNSCORED for every run, which is not a pass and was guarding
nothing at all. Re-measuring at fc07fef6 against the same video-on
reference set moves 21 of the 30 numbers. Only ONE moved enough to have
breached its old ceiling:
FEP_MAIN@settled lang-selector  17.19 -> 25.41  (+8.22pp, BREACH of the
19.19 ceiling the stale block implied). This is NOT flake: our own
cross-run variance is confined to bg-emblem-topright and does not touch
this region, and both HEAD captures read 25.41 exactly. It is a real
regression in the released language row, carried forward here as the
recorded fact rather than hidden by leaving the gate abstaining.
Also worse, all within the old ceilings: title-logo @settled 29.48 ->
31.46, @reveal 31.83 -> 33.08; bg-emblem-topright @settled 19.92 ->
21.23, @reveal 22.97 -> 23.77; version-overlay @reveal 9.12 -> 10.13;
lang-selector @reveal 61.55 -> 63.53. Better: menu-column @settled 23.35
-> 19.32, decor-left-arc @settled 12.15 -> 11.33, FEP_MAIN@entry FULL
FRAME 7.53 -> 7.44 and title-logo 22.17 -> 21.67.
captureDeterminism: CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (task #150). This block used to claim 'Our own
contribution to run-to-run variance is 0.00%', measured from two
byte-identical mainmenu captures of 684c7c52. That is NO LONGER TRUE at
fc07fef6: two back-to-back production captures of the same commit differ
on ALL 161 frames. The difference is small and localised - 275 pixels per
frame (0.09% material at a >2/255 threshold), every one of them inside
x 418-442, y 4-29, which lies in bg-emblem-topright.
Its effect on the gated statistic is bounded and measured: across the two
runs, 27 of the 30 numbers are IDENTICAL, and the three that move are
bg-emblem-topright (<=0.42pp) and the FULL FRAME that contains it
(<=0.07pp). No other region varies at all.
So the 2.00pp margin still covers our own variance with room to spare -
but it is now an allowance for measured flake in ONE region as well as
headroom, and that must not be forgotten the next time someone reasons
about widening or narrowing it. The mechanism of the 275-pixel wobble is
NOT established and is not claimed here.
THE MARGIN DOES NOT NEED TO COVER RETAIL'S CROSS-RUN FLOOR, and must not be
widened on the argument that it should. That floor reaches 8.95% on
lang-selector @settled and 7.15% on bg-empty-left @settled, both far above
2.00pp - but the gated statistic is gapPct, which discards floor-unstable
pixels ONE AT A TIME before counting. The floor is already gone from the
number the ceiling bounds.

_windowNote: FEP_MAIN is gated as THREE windows rather than one, because retail builds
the page up in stages and a single window would hide a regression behind
the stage we are worst at.
Measured 2026-07-27 from the retail run1 burst, region mean RGB:
t000014  lang-selector, menu-column and the arcs are ALL exactly the
flat fill (23,23,48). Only title-logo and bg-emblem-topright
are drawn. Retail's first main-menu frame carries background
plus logo plus emblem and NOTHING ELSE.
t000524  all chrome present and over-bright (lang-selector 66,82,122)
t001020+ settling to its steady value (lang-selector 58,52,74)
SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28, and left here because the reasoning is why the three
windows exist. This read: 'We draw the entire page on frame 0, which is why
the entry window scores 76% gap against a retail cross-run floor of 0.24% -
retail is perfectly reproducible there and we simply differ. That is a real
defect, tracked separately.' It WAS, and 8618e773 closed it by porting
retail's 50-frame staged reveal: the entry window is now 7.53% against the
same 0.24% floor, and seven of its nine named regions are at or under 0.30%.
The three windows earned their keep exactly as intended. A single window
would have averaged a 76% defect into a ~20% page and hidden it, and the
same split now keeps the settled window sensitive at its own ~15% scale
while the entry window gates at 7.53%.

_samplesNote: Every settled retail run1 burst offset, not the five the hand
measurements used. The extra seven cost a few seconds and they are
the ones that would catch a phase regression that happens to look
fine at the five offsets a human picked.

unscored.reason: the missing piece is no longer the reference. Task #150 captured retail's options pages WITH the video backdrop in two runs (local-lab/retail-reference-pristine/nofmv-options-2026-07-31/run1 and run2, 17 burst frames each for optroot/optctrl/optsound/optvideo/credits plus mm), so a noise floor now exists. What blocks gating is OUR side: FrontendCaptureRig's OptionsPlan takes ONE settled shot per page (fep-options-root.png and friends), while this plan pairs frames by millisecond offset from `<prefix>-t<ms>ms.png`. There is nothing to pair against a burst. Gating the options pages needs the rig to sweep them the way it sweeps mainmenu; until then rebuild/tools/compare_options_capture.py's ink-mask IoU is the only options measurement, and it is a text-placement check, not a parity score.
retail's own two runs disagree by 5.8-44.2% material at matched page-entry offsets, so no reconstruction improvement below that is measurable. Gating on it would be theatre.
